title: Harmonize top_k semantics, candidate provenance, and paged rerank responses
creator: Maeve Chen
description:
Background: Customer teams frequently use the rerank endpoint to re-score a set of retrieval candidates. Current behaviors are inconsistent across clients: 'top_k' sometimes refers to how many candidates we score internally and sometimes to how many are returned; pagination cursors can yield different orderings between pages; structured output is underspecified so downstream apps rehydrate candidate provenance from best-effort fields. This ticket standardizes semantics and the schema to improve developer ergonomics, reduce accidental regressions, and make pagination scalable and deterministic.

Goals: 1) Define unambiguous top_k semantics: differentiate 'k_return' (number of items returned to caller) and 'k_score' (how many candidates to score internally) with sensible defaults. 2) Extend input schema to carry candidate provenance/metadata and optional precomputed embeddings. 3) Produce a structured and stable output with explicit score normalization, tie-break rules, and a stateless cursor scheme that guarantees deterministic pagination for the same input + model version. 4) Keep migration path for existing clients (v1) and enable gradual rollout. 5) Meet latency and scaling targets for common workloads (k_return <= 10, input candidates <= 200).

Proposed API changes (high level):
- Request: add top-level fields k_return (optional), k_score (optional), and rerank_mode ("score_then_sort" | "sort_then_score"), and allow per-candidate metadata object {id, source, precomputed_embedding?}. Allow batch queries (list of query objects) where each query can provide candidates or a candidate set id.
- Response: return 'items' as array of objects {candidate_id, source, score, score_normalized, rank, tie_breaker_code, values_explaining_score?}. Include 'cursor' string for pagination that encodes deterministic state and server-side model_version/tag. Cursors are opaque but include a server-signed digest to prevent tampering. Provide 'approx_total' when available.
- Versioning: New schema under header X-Redwood-Rerank-Version: 2 or ?version=2 query param. Default remains v1 until opt-in rollouts finish.

Performance & correctness constraints:
- If k_score is omitted, server defaults to max(k_return, 64) with a hard cap when candidate_set_size is large.
- Pagination must not re-order already-returned items: subsequent pages must present remaining items in deterministic order given same model_version and same input.
- For streaming use-cases we will support a 'streaming_mode' that emits pages as soon as they are available while preserving deterministic rank semantics for items emitted later.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Compatibility & rollout: Implement feature-flag controlled V2. When disabled, server behaves as today. When enabled, server accepts v2 requests and returns v2 responses. Migration docs will detail mapping rules from v1 to v2 and recommended client changes.

Testing & evals: end-to-end perf tests with candidate set sizes [10, 50, 200, 1000], unit tests for cursor stability, fuzz tests for cursor tampering, and quality regression tests using existing rerank eval suites.

Success metrics: reduce "incorrect pagination" bug reports to zero for new v2 requests, maintain p95 latency within 1.5x current baseline for small k, and reduce overall per-token CPU by 15% via optimized early-filter path for precomputed embeddings.
acceptance_criteria: API spec doc published for v2 (confluence) with examples for simple and batched requests
Server implements k_return/k_score fields and honors defaults documented above
Deterministic opaque cursor implemented; same input+model_version produces identical paged results
Structured response includes score_normalized and tie_breaker_code fields
Integration tests covering candidate sizes 10/50/200 and both streaming and paged modes
Migration doc and compatibility header published; SDK patch for Python and Node released behind feature flag
Performance targets validated in perf dashboard: p50 <= 25ms for k_return<=10, p95 <= 120ms for common small sets
decisions: Adopt explicit k_return (user-facing) and k_score (internal) separation to avoid ambiguity
Use opaque, server-signed cursor rather than index-based cursors to prevent tampering and to encode model_version
Include candidate provenance (source and id) in both request and response to help downstream tracing and A/B analysis
Default k_score to max(k_return, 64) to balance quality and latency for typical workloads
tradeoffs: Opaque signed cursors increase server encode/decode work and require storage of short-lived metadata, but provide stronger guarantees vs stateless offsets
Returning richer structured output increases payload size; to mitigate, provide a compact mode and allow clients to opt into verbose 'explain' fields
Tighter deterministic ordering ties system complexity with fallback logic when model_version changes mid-pagination; we will surface clear errors when model mismatches occur
